manifest_name: Mapping With Melanin — Inclusive Public-Art Stage 1 Candidate Manifest

scope.media_policy: No source photography, image files, hotlinks, or generated depictions are included.

candidates.street_address_or_precise_public_locatio: Gordon White Park, Ralph David Abernathy Boulevard SW and White Street SW, Atlanta, GA 30310
candidates.access_notes: The City of Atlanta collection describes the sculpture at Gordon White Park and invites viewers to walk around it. Park-hour and current-condition confirmation is still required before a future publication decision.
candidates.work_status: Documented in the City of Atlanta public-art archive as a 1977 sculpture; current on-site condition was not field-verified in Stage 1.
candidates.source_publisher: City of Atlanta Mayor's Office of Cultural Affairs
candidates.artist_evidence_note: The City collection page credits Curtis Patterson directly.
candidates.location_evidence_note: The City collection page names Gordon White Park and gives the Ralph David Abernathy Boulevard SW / White Street SW intersection. Dry-run coordinates were derived from that public intersection, not from imagery.
candidates.community_context_evidence_note: The City collection page states that the abstract sculpture 'draws heavily on African motifs.' This records the source's description of the work, not an inference about the artist.
candidates.source_rights_note: The source page is used for factual provenance only. It does not grant MWM permission to reuse its photography or other media.
candidates.missing_evidence_reason: No critical source-field gap found, but current access/work condition must be confirmed and the owner-approved public-art metadata/canonical-route work is required before any import.
candidates.future_publication_missing_evidence_reas: The record has a complete Tier 1 source, but cannot be safely imported until the approved public-art metadata model and canonical-route integration exist and a current access/work-status check is completed.

candidates.artist_display_name: Ernel Martinez; Felix St. Fort; Parris Stancell
candidates.access_notes: Mural Arts lists the work as 'On View.' The source describes the large mural on a Haitian church at the recorded address.
candidates.work_status: On View, according to Mural Arts Philadelphia.
candidates.artist_evidence_note: Mural Arts lists Ernel Martinez, Felix St. Fort, and Parris Stancell; its project narrative identifies Felix St. Fort and Ernel Martinez as designers of the large mural and Parris Stancell as a collaborator.
candidates.location_evidence_note: Mural Arts lists 4675 Germantown Avenue and supplies the recorded latitude/longitude in its location link.
candidates.community_context_evidence_note: Mural Arts documents collaboration with eighteen Haitian earthquake survivors and the larger Haitian population in Germantown; it identifies Haitian cultural references in the mural. This records the publisher's language without assigning identity to artists from names or appearance.
candidates.source_rights_note: The Mural Arts project page is a factual source only. No Mural Arts images or other media may be reused without separate permission or a documented license.
candidates.missing_evidence_reason: A complete Tier 2 record requires an independent Tier 1 or second independent corroborating source for future owner review; the current metadata/route gap also blocks import.
candidates.future_publication_missing_evidence_reas: The source is a complete Tier 2 project record, but the future-publication rule requires a complete Tier 1 source or independent corroboration covering location and attribution/context. The current schema/route gap also blocks import.

candidates.street_address_or_precise_public_locatio: 6014 South Cottage Grove Avenue, Chicago, IL
candidates.access_notes: Chicago Public Art Group documents a sculpture completed and installed at this street address in 2019, but Stage 1 did not obtain an independent current-access or condition confirmation. Do not present it as currently viewable until that check is completed.
candidates.work_status: Documented as completed and installed in March 2019; current physical-status confirmation remains required.
candidates.artist_evidence_note: Chicago Public Art Group credits Bernard Williams in its Artist section.
candidates.location_evidence_note: Chicago Public Art Group lists 6014 South Cottage Grove Avenue. The dry-run coordinates were geocoded from that source-supplied public address and must not be treated as a field survey.
candidates.community_context_display: African textiles and carvings; Afri-COBRA artists in Woodlawn
candidates.community_context_evidence_note: Chicago Public Art Group explains that the work's pattern designs originate in African textiles and carvings and refer to Afri-COBRA artists based in Woodlawn. This records documented source context rather than inferring the artist's identity.
candidates.source_rights_note: The project page is used for factual provenance only. Its imagery and media are not licensed to MWM by this manifest.
candidates.missing_evidence_reason: A second independent source must corroborate location and attribution/context, current access/work status must be confirmed, and the owner-approved public-art metadata/canonical-route work is required before any import.
candidates.future_publication_missing_evidence_reas: A second independent source must corroborate location and attribution/context, and current access/work status must be confirmed. The current schema/route gap also blocks import.
